The Solaredge integration does not provide any useful statistics for the new energy features in 2021.08 except for "lifetime energy".

It is my understanding that this is due to the integration not yet supporting these new features in HA as per [this link](https://www.home-assistant.io/more-info/statistics/), hence this issue.

_No response_

@odgregg it's not a good idea to use the integration sensor as a workaround, the data will always be incorrect. Main reason is that you integrate based on sensors that are updated every 10 minutes (default API polling) on HA's side, while solaredge uses live data consistently to compute imported and exported Wh. You can see this if you use the solaredge app or website, data is updated in real-time as you turn on/off appliances around your home.
So the sensors from the integration need to be adapted to report the last_reset value, based on the real exact time these sensors are reset on solaredge's side.

Hi,

I made progress with the integration platform (thanks @Spartan-II-117), but ran afoul of the need to have two separate KwH sensors (one for power going into and one for power leaving the battery).  SolarEdge gives one value, which is negative for power going into the battery and positive for power leaving.   I just made two KwH sensors with a template and thought that would give me what I need for the Energy tab.

Both KwH sensors are working, but the Energy tab won't recognize `to_battery_kwh`!  So near yet so far.

Details:

Here are the sensors I created:
```
  - platform: template
    sensors:
      to_battery_kw:
        unit_of_measurement: "kW"
        device_class: energy
        friendly_name: "Kw going to battery for Energy Tab"
        value_template: >-
          {% if ((states("sensor.solaredge_storage_power")|float) > 0 ) %}
            0.0
          {% else %}
            {{ -(states("sensor.solaredge_storage_power")|float) }}
          {% endif %}

  - platform: template
    sensors:
      from_battery_kw:
        unit_of_measurement: "kW"
        device_class: energy

to anyone using an solaredge inverter, I would recommend to use the "SolarEdge Modbus" in addition to the default solaredge integration.

also, getting values such as current production, and so on in a higher frequency, and more reliable connection (since the connection relies only on your local network) the whole thing seems more sustainable and stable to me.
